npcs.name: Fiona the Harper
npcs.idle: Lorcan wrote me a poem every day for a year. Then he wrote them for someone else.

npcs.name: Old Sadhbh
npcs.idle: I've keened for three chieftains. The banshee keened first, every time.

npcs.name: Steward Conn
npcs.idle: The Chieftess is well. Perfectly well. Please don't trouble her.

quests.title: The Lhiannan-Sidhe
quests.offer:
Lorcan was my lover and the finest poet in Cullen. Last spring a lhiannan-sidhe found him - a faerie muse. They give a poet the best verses he'll ever write, and they drink his life to do it.

He wrote to me last month, from somewhere in the bog. The writing was an old man's. He's thirty. Will you [find Lorcan]?
quests.summary: A lhiannan-sidhe - a faerie muse who feeds on poets - has taken Fiona's lover into the bog.

steps.goal: Go into the bog by the siabra tower
steps.text: Siabra watch from the tower. Pages of verse are stuck to the reeds, soaked, the ink running.

clue.name: pages of verse in a shaking hand

steps.text: Each page better than the last, and each hand older. The last pages are nearly illegible - and nearly perfect.

steps.goal: Cut through the bog creepers to the east

steps.say:
Fiona sent you. Fiona. I wrote her a hundred poems and none of them were good enough. Now I write for HER, and every one is perfect.

She'll come at dusk. Look at me. I'm thirty. I don't care. I don't care. Do you understand - every [word]...

steps.text: The lhiannan-sidhe falls back, hissing, into the mist. Lorcan clutches his chest and breathes like a man surfacing from deep water.

stages.name: the Lhiannan-Sidhe
stages.announce: A woman more beautiful than the moon walks out of the mist. 'He is mine. He is my masterpiece.'

steps.goal: Decide what becomes of the verses
steps.say:
She's not gone. Not while I have the verses. They're hers as much as mine - she lives in them. If I [burn the verses], I'm free, and I'll go back to Fiona and write bad poems and grow old slowly.

If I [keep them], she'll come back, and I'll die before winter, and they'll sing these in every hall in Hibernia for a thousand years. Choose. Please. I can't.

options.say: ...They burn so slowly. ...There. I can't remember a line. Not one. Take me to Fiona.
Then I'll keep them. Tell Fiona the best ones are hers. They are. Tell her I'm sorry.

steps.say: He's home. He's grey and thin and he can't remember a word he wrote - and he wrote me a poem this morning. It's terrible. It's the best thing I've ever read.

He kept them. And he sent me the best ones.

They're... they're beyond anything. I'll set them to music. I'll play them at his wake, which will be before winter. Take this, and go, before I cry on you.

burned.text: Take this. He wanted you to.

quests.title: The Keening
quests.offer:
This is GROUP work, so bring friends you trust.

The banshee of Cullen has keened under the Chieftess' window every night for a week. A banshee keens for a death in the old families. But nobody is sick. Nobody is old. Nobody's dying.

When a banshee keens for a death that hasn't come, it's because someone means to make it come. Will you [find out who]? Start with the [steward]. He's too calm.

topics.steward: Conn. He runs the Chieftess' household. He's very calm. Far too calm.

quests.summary: GROUP. The banshee of Cullen keens nightly for the Chieftess - who isn't sick. Someone means her death.

steps.say:
The banshee? Old women's stories. The Chieftess is perfectly well. I see to everything - her food, her wine, her guests. I'd know if anything were wrong.

If you must poke about, the black wraiths in the bog to the [east] have been bold of late. Go and deal with them. That would actually be useful.

steps.goal: Deal with the black wraiths east of town
steps.text: Among the wraith-mud, a dropped satchel - a steward's satchel, with a steward's seal.
A vial of sidhe glass, nearly empty. A letter: 'Half in her wine each night. By the dark moon it will look like a wasting. The venator will finish it if it doesn't. - C.'
A grey woman sits on a stone in the bog, combing her hair, weeping. She looks up at you.

steps.say:
You hear me. Good. Few do, before.

The Chieftess' death is close. The steward pours it. And the siabra hunter waits in the bog to the west of my stone, to finish it if the poison is slow. Stop the [hunter]. I am so tired of keening.

steps.goal: Kill the siabra assassin in the bog
steps.text: The venator dies in the bog-water. Far off, under the Chieftess' window, the keening stops.

stages.name: Iuchra the Venator
stages.announce: A siabra in mud-grey leathers rises out of the bog with a knife in each hand. 'The steward pays well. You'll do for practice.'

steps.say:
The keening's stopped. I heard it stop at moonrise. And you have the vial. Conn.

Conn, who has served her twenty years. He wanted the chieftainship for his son - it's in his letters.

The Chieftess is too kind. She'll want to [banish him]. The old law says [death] for a poisoner. She'll ask me, and I'll ask you. You've seen more of it than I have.

options.say: Banished. Beyond the Shannon, with nothing but his cloak. ...She'll weep for him. She's like that.
The old law, then. I'll keen for him myself. Somebody should.

banished.text: From the Chieftess, with her thanks.
